main_text.p: qui aureus asservatur in monasterio Lætiensi in Hannoniâ, quem ecce habes.
[woodcut illustration: Crucifixion medallion with Greek legend; not transcribed as text]

Inscriptio in eo est : Κόσμε τὸ λύτρον, αἷμα τῆς Θεῖς Λόγῳ : Mundi redemptio, sanguis Dei Verbi. Missus is nummus cum aliis sacris donariis est ab Henrico Imperatore, tunc Constantinopoli, anno Christi MCIↃ.CC.VIII.

page.notes: The Greek legend on the medallion is set in the scan as ΚΟΣΜΟΥ ΤΟ ΛΥΤΡΟΝ / ΑΙΜΑ ΤΟΥ ΘΕΟΥ ΛΟΓΟΥ; the Greek in the inscription line is partly worn and transcribed as best read. The date "cIↄ. cc. viii." is read as printed in the scan (MCC VIII form); the year 1208 is uncertain in its numerals. The woodcut itself is described, not transcribed. The "AD" at the foot is a printed word/mark, possibly a catchword or signature fragment.
